teaser.text: Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group is a Chinese prescription-drug company: it discovers, makes and sells medicines, with cancer treatment at its center. To understand its business, follow renminbi from a patient’s treatment through distributors and partners into Hansoh’s accounts, then out again through research, manufacturing, selling and operations.

stock.title: Hansoh stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Hansoh stock forecast: weighted scenarios, key drivers, real free cash flow and today's valuation.
stock.opening: Hansoh's weighted forecast reaches HKD30.98 in October 2029. It hinges on durable product growth and successful pipeline execution.
stock.closing: The full Hansoh memo also covers Hansoh's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted forecast implies modest downside first, then recovery toward today’s price. The weighted price is HKD27.90 in October 2027, a negative 11% return including dividends. It rises to HKD29.35 in October 2028, still a negative 5% return. By October 2029, it reaches HKD30.98, a positive 2% return.
The weighted forecast points to modest downside before recovery toward today’s price by October 2029, hinging on durable product growth and successful pipeline execution.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Hansoh, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: This path reflects recent growth, but excludes the identified investment gain and assumes no conditional milestone becomes recurring profit. Innovative medicines and collaborative products were 82.2% of 2025 revenue, while oncology contributed 66.4%, so product growth is credible but concentrated. The bear case falls to CNY5,580m by 2029 as pricing, uptake and launches disappoint. The bull case reaches CNY10,080m if approvals and new indications make product growth outpace R&D and selling costs.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Hansoh really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow starts with profit and adjusts for non-cash items and movements in items such as receivables, inventories and customer advances. Free cash flow goes further by deducting capital spending, lease payments and interest. The table’s “real” free cash flow also removes stock-based compensation, giving a stricter view of cash available to the business.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Hansoh?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, shows how much investors pay for each unit of profit. A forward P/E uses expected profit, so it is a forecast rather than a fact. The important question is what produces that profit. Product sales can recur as patients continue using medicines. Collaboration revenue usually comes from a licensing or partnership deal, while interest comes from investing cash. All three can raise accounting profit, but they do not carry the same promise of repetition.

blocks.heading: How much does Hansoh pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Hansoh paid dividends every year shown. In 2025, shareholder payouts were RMB2,012.184 million. The rest of that year’s free cash flow stayed available for research, licensing, facilities or reserves. Hansoh also generated RMB6,738 million from operations in 2025 and spent RMB458 million on capital expenditure, mainly workshops and equipment.

paragraphs.text: Hansoh’s real free cash flow margin rose across the five-year period and reached 41.4% in 2025. Hansoh’s real free cash flow per share reached RMB1.04, above diluted EPS of RMB0.93. RMB0.73 remained after dividends and buybacks; net cash rose across the five years shown.

paragraphs.text: The dividend base case increases from CNY0.40 to CNY0.48 per share as marketed-product growth supports distributions, but R&D and uneven collaboration income restrain the pace. The bear case cuts the dividend to CNY0.26, while the bull case raises it to CNY0.59. The base starts above the 2025 equivalent of about CNY0.367 and reflects the higher 2026 interim declaration.

The bull case would gain weight if pivotal data lead to applications and approvals, followed by hospital access and sustained prescribing. Faster dividend growth would support the view if operating cash flow improves. Partner milestones would matter most in 2028–2029 because they could validate future royalties.

paragraphs.text: The final-date outcomes are wide. The bear case is HKD12.94 and the bull case is HKD61.30. Today’s price is HKD31.74, so the model offers substantial downside risk alongside a large upside tail.
